stories.why_ar: كلّها بالمضارع البسيط وفعل to be — أوّل نادرة لجحا تقرؤها كاملة بالإنجليزية.
lines: It is night, and Juha is at the well.
He looks down into the dark water.
Oh no, the moon is in the well!
"Poor moon," Juha says. "I can help."
He gets a long rope and a hook.
He pulls and pulls, and he falls down.
Now Juha is on his back.
He can see the moon in the sky.
"Good," he says. "The moon is home again."
stories.moral_en: Sometimes we help in a funny way.

stories.why_ar: تكرار «يسحب ويسحب» يرسّخ المضارع البسيط وطلب المساعدة بـ can.
lines: In an old man's garden, a turnip grows and grows.
Now it is big. It is very, very big!
The old man pulls and pulls. No.
"Help me, please!" he says to his wife.
She pulls the man, and the man pulls the turnip. No.
Then their granddaughter comes, and the dog, and the cat.
They pull and pull and pull. No!
Then a little mouse runs in. "Can I help?"
The cat laughs, but the mouse pulls the cat's tail.
One, two, three... POP! Out comes the turnip!
Everyone sits down on the ground and laughs.
Tonight there is turnip soup, and the first bowl is for the mouse.
stories.moral_en: A small hand can finish a big job.
stories.moral_ar: يدٌ صغيرة قد تُكمل عملاً كبيراً.

stories.why_ar: سؤال «Who can help me…?» يتكرّر، فتتدرّب على الأسئلة وعلى can.
lines: The little red hen finds wheat seeds.
"Who can help me plant them?" she asks.
"Not I," say the dog, the cat, and the duck.
"Then I can do it alone," says the hen.
The wheat grows tall and gold.
"Who can help me cut it?" "Not I, not I, not I."
"Who can help me make the bread?" "Not I, not I, not I."
So the hen makes the bread alone.
Mmm! The bread smells good.
"Who can help me eat it?" asks the hen.
"I can!" says the dog. "I can!" say the cat and the duck.
"No," says the hen. "Today I can do it alone."

stories.why_ar: there is وthere are وصفات مثل hot وcold وsoft في قالب يتكرّر: كبير، ثم متوسّط، ثم صغير.
lines: A girl with gold hair walks into a house in the forest.
Nobody is home, but there are three bowls on the table.
The big bowl is too hot. The middle bowl is too cold.
The little bowl is just right, so she eats it all.
Upstairs, there are three beds.
The big bed is too hard. The middle bed is too soft.
The little bed is just right, so she sleeps.
Then the door opens. Three bears are home!
"Where is my soup?" asks Baby Bear. "It isn't here!"
Upstairs, he cries, "Look! There is a girl in my bed!"
The girl jumps up and runs, runs, runs.
stories.moral_en: Not your house, not your bed.

stories.source_ar: حكاية شعبية أمريكية وإنجليزية — أُعيدت كتابتها
stories.why_ar: لازمة «You can't catch me!» تدرّبك على can وcan't وصيغة الأمر.
lines: An old woman makes a gingerbread man.
She opens the oven, and he jumps out!
"Run, run, as fast as you can! You can't catch me!"
The old woman runs, but she can't catch him.
A cow runs, and a horse runs. They can't catch him.
Then he comes to a wide river. Oh no, he can't swim!
A fox smiles. "Sit on my tail. I can help you."
In the water, the fox says, "Sit on my back. It is dry."
Then he says, "Sit on my nose. It is very dry."
The gingerbread man sits on the fox's nose.
SNAP! That is the end.
stories.moral_en: Be careful of a sweet smile.

stories.why_ar: حكاية قديمة بجمل قصيرة، مع can وcan't.
lines: A fox is in a garden.
He is hungry, and he is thirsty.
There are grapes on a tall tree.
They are big, purple, and sweet.
The fox jumps, but he can't get them.
He jumps again and again.
He is tired now, and he sits down.
"Those grapes are bad," he says.
"I don't want them. They are sour."
stories.moral_en: It is easy to hate what you can't have.
stories.moral_ar: من السهل أن تكره ما لا تقدر عليه.

stories.why_ar: نادرة معروفة بالمضارع البسيط، وفيها أفعال يوميّة كثيرة.
lines: Juha is at a big dinner in old clothes.
Nobody talks to him or gives him food.
He goes home and puts on a new coat.
Then he comes back to the dinner.
Now everyone says, "Welcome, sit here!"
They give him meat, rice, and soup.
Juha puts the food on his coat.
"Eat, my coat, eat," he says.
"You are the guest here, not me."

stories.source_ar: حكاية صينية من كتاب جوانغ تزو — أُعيدت كتابتها
stories.why_ar: there is والأسئلة البسيطة مثل Where do you live? في حوار قصير بين ضفدع وسلحفاة.
lines: A little frog lives in an old well.
"My home is the whole world," he says.
He looks up. The sky is small and round, like a coin.
One day, a sea turtle comes to the well.
"Come in!" says the frog. "There is water, there is mud. I have everything!"
The turtle tries, but his foot is too big.
"Where do you live?" asks the frog.
"In the sea," says the turtle. "It is blue, and it has no end."
"No end?" The frog laughs. "That is not possible."
Then he looks up at his little round sky.
And for a long time, the frog is quiet.
stories.moral_en: Your sky is only as big as your well.

stories.title_en: How the Camel Got His Hump
stories.source_ar: روديارد كبلنغ، حكايات «هكذا تماماً» — أُعيدت كتابتها
stories.why_ar: صيغة الأمر مثل Come and work! والمضارع البسيط، مع لازمة مضحكة: Humph!
lines: The world is new, and every animal works.
The horse carries people, and the dog helps the man.
But the camel sits in the desert and eats.
"Come and work with us!" says the horse. "Humph!" says the camel.
"Come and help us!" says the dog. "Humph!"
"Come and work!" says the ox. "Humph!"
So the three tired animals go to the Djinn of the desert.
The Djinn looks at the camel and says a magic word.
Suddenly, the camel's back grows big and round: a humph!
"Now you can work three days with no food," says the Djinn.
And that is why the camel has a hump today.
stories.moral_en: Run from work, and work finds you.
stories.moral_ar: من يهرب من العمل يلحقه العمل.

stories.why_ar: حكاية عن ردّ الجميل بجمل من خمس كلمات أو ستّ.
lines: A little ant is very thirsty.
She goes to the river for water.
She falls in, and she can't swim.
A dove in a tree sees her.
The dove drops a leaf into the water.
The ant gets on the leaf.
Now she is safe on the grass.
"Thank you, dove," she says. "You are kind."
"Now we are friends," says the dove.

stories.title_en: Ali Baba and the Magic Word
stories.source_ar: من حكايات ألف ليلة وليلة — أُعيدت كتابتها
stories.why_ar: there is وcan't وصيغة الأمر Open, Sesame! في أشهر حكايات ألف ليلة.
lines: Ali Baba is a poor man with a donkey.
He sees forty thieves at a big rock.
"Open, Sesame!" says the leader, and the rock opens!
Inside, there is gold, gold, and more gold.
The thieves ride away, and Ali Baba goes to the rock.
"Open, Sesame!" he says, and he takes a little gold.
His rich brother Qasim hears about the cave.
Qasim goes in and fills bag after bag with gold.
But now he can't remember the magic word.
"Open, Wheat! Open, Rice! Open, Bean!" Nothing.
Outside, he can hear the horses of the thieves.
Poor Qasim! The word is a little seed.
stories.moral_en: A greedy head forgets the small things.

stories.why_ar: حكاية عن المديح الكاذب، كلّها بالمضارع وفعل to be.
lines: A black crow is in a tree.
She has a piece of cheese.
A fox looks up at the crow.
"You are very beautiful," he says.
"Your eyes are bright, and your wings shine."
"Can you sing for me, please?"
The crow is happy, and she opens her mouth.
The cheese falls down to the fox.
"Thank you," says the fox, and he runs away.
